title: Narratives, context and funding speed
audience: Portfolio and industry readers, using a Kiva/partner decision case

slides.title:
Narratives, context
and funding speed
slides.subtitle: A research decision case from 1.45 million Kiva records
slides.message: Measure what narratives add, then test whether a truthful change helps.
slides.evidence: Verified saved primary results and reviewed October sensitivity. Cultural Blend was one of eight finalists.
slides.visual: Minimal editorial cover, team names and recognition; no model-performance claim.
slides.action: Understand the project as a decision case with an explicit next test.
slides.notes: We are Mike Nguyen and Sophia Nguyen from Cultural Blend. This case began with a marketing question: which loan narratives are associated with faster funding? The maintained research now asks a more useful next question: what information does text add, and what evidence would justify changing how a loan is presented? We distinguish what the competition work established from later research.

slides.title: Prioritise a fair text comparison and a targeted pilot
items: Validate the outcome, text measures and listing-time information.
Measure what text adds beyond loan and market context.
Evaluate one factual presentation change with participating partners.
slides.message: The immediate recommendation is a sequence of evidence-building decisions.
slides.evidence: Source audit found an unsupported narrative-free claim; existing inference is observational and context-sensitive.
slides.visual: Three large numbered statements on a flat canvas; no invented impact scores.
slides.action: Approve the research sequence before commissioning additional model complexity.
slides.notes: The first investment should address the biggest uncertainty: whether narrative information adds stable value once the loan context is known. Then we can ask whether a particular factual presentation change improves outcomes. These are recommendations for research actions. We have not measured a return on investment or an intervention effect.

slides.title: The outcome is completed funding on the platform
slides.message: The observed sample and timing determine what the project can claim.
slides.evidence: 1,453,846 input rows; six negative durations excluded; 1,453,840 eligible, including 1,637 refunded records. Dictionary reports 96.4% pre-disbursal.
slides.visual: Large eligible count at left, listing-to-completion timeline in text at right, precise population footnote.
slides.action: Interpret later results within completed records and distinguish borrower disbursal.
slides.notes: The full input contains 1,453,846 records from 2016 to 2025. Six negative durations are excluded. The analysis includes 1,637 refunded records with valid completed durations. The dictionary's full-data descriptive audit reports 96.4% pre-disbursal, so listing-to-completion time often begins after money has already been disbursed. It does not directly measure borrower waiting, partner liquidity or welfare. Unfunded and expired listings are needed to study all-listing success.

slides.title: Investigate four connected parts of the funding process
rows: Verified partner ID and process history
slides.message: Choose a mechanism to investigate before choosing a lever to change.
slides.evidence: Repository schema and Kiva process documentation; missing fields are data requests, not established causes.
slides.visual: Native editable issue-tree matrix with observed versus missing evidence.
slides.action: Prioritise the missing data required by the intended intervention.
slides.notes: This issue tree is a working decomposition. Its branches interact: a partner's process may affect both wording and exposure. Literature gives reasons to consider prosocial framing and lender preferences, while Kiva describes editing and translation in the posting process. None of these mechanisms is identified by a predictive importance chart. We should request data that can distinguish them.

slides.title: Saved forecasts show signal among completed loans
slides.message: Prediction is useful evidence of information content, but does not isolate the contribution of text.
slides.visual: Native editable MAE bar chart with zero baseline and three models. Classifier AUC/AP at right. Explicit completed-record population.
slides.action: Accept the historical benchmark and request the missing controlled comparison.
slides.notes: The saved August pipeline outperformed its training-median baseline on later completed loans. The nonlinear duration model reduced MAE from 8.72 to 5.20 days, and the 24-hour classifier had AUC 0.900 and average precision 0.830. This compares model configurations, not a structural-only model with an otherwise identical text-added model. It therefore cannot quantify text's added value. These are saved metrics, not a new run. The posting-date split also needs a label-availability audit before a stronger historical-deployment claim.

slides.title: The missing experiment is the incremental value of text
rows: Can the model beat an available simple forecast?
What does text encode, including context?
Same model plus staged text blocks
Does text add value after proxy context?
slides.message: Same rows, model family, chronology and tuning budget make the comparison interpretable.
slides.evidence: Notebook 2 uses narrative features in every predictive fit. Historical Ridge ablation is narrower and not a fresh October prediction run.
slides.visual: Comparison design table, not simulated performance bars.
slides.action: Run the matched comparison before saying that structure dominates or text adds little.
slides.notes: The notebook's claim that the classifier needs no narrative features contradicts its input matrix. We should correct that claim immediately in the next notebook revision. The primary research experiment uses matched feature blocks within the same model family. Text-only performance is diagnostic because text can encode country, purpose and programme. The key quantity is the paired difference between structure plus text and structure alone, with uncertainty and a practical threshold. Compare S versus S+text and S+P versus S+P+text on the same rows. P is an unvalidated programme-text proxy; these contrasts do not identify confounding removed or partner effects.

slides.title: Large row counts do not remove contextual uncertainty
slides.message: Regional narrative patterns require careful treatment of the number of independent countries.
slides.evidence: Middle East slope −.0729, normal interval [−.1003,−.0456], heuristic [−.2502,.1043], 2 countries; Central America −.0742, normal [−.0879,−.0605], heuristic [−.1629,.0145], 2 countries. Slope units: change in log(1+days) per additional family mention per 100 words.
slides.visual: Two-region native table with point estimates, normal intervals and heuristic intervals. Clearly label the latter as uncalibrated sensitivity.
slides.action: Treat regional patterns as exploratory hypotheses, not country-specific writing advice.
slides.notes: The two regional point estimates suggest faster completed funding with more family mentions, conditional on the primary model. Each pooled region contains only two countries. The normal-reference country-clustered intervals and the much wider t(1) screen show why the uncertainty deserves attention. The screen is heuristic and is not a calibrated correction. In the same primary analysis, urgency has country-clustered p=.4943 for duration and .2233 for 24-hour completion. Failure to reject does not establish a negligible effect.

slides.title: Later checks retain some narrative associations
slides.after: Programme-adjusted business framing, 24-hour completion: −0.258 pp per additional mention / 100 words; 95% interval [−0.390, −0.126] pp; adjusted p = 0.00635.
slides.message: Statistical support changes with specification; a universal editing benefit remains unestablished.
slides.evidence: Same 1,453,840 eligible rows and 48 countries across four fits. Joint framing families remain associated. Primary predictive models were not rerun.
slides.visual: Compact specification comparison plus one clearly unit-labelled 24-hour result. Keep the two outcomes separate.
slides.action: Retire the blanket null story while retaining the intervention boundary.
slides.notes: The October extension is later research, separate from the competition submission. The third-person duration estimate changes modestly, while its adjusted p-value crosses .05. This is not proof that the association disappeared. Business framing is associated with a lower 24-hour completion probability under the programme specification. Several joint families remain associated. The programme variable is a text-derived proxy, not a verified partner ID. Coefficients are per extra mention per 100 words, and the duration outcome is log(1+days). Multiplicity is handled within each outcome/specification, not across the entire research history. Duration pointwise 95% intervals are [−0.013833, −0.004183] for expanded controls and [−0.013210, −0.002965] for programme adjustment. Business framing has a pointwise interval [−0.390, −0.126] percentage points. Intervals are pointwise; the displayed p-values are BH-adjusted within each outcome/specification.

slides.title: Choose actions by evidence and readiness
rows: Defer rollout until data and policy checks
slides.message: Prioritise learning value without inventing intervention returns.
slides.evidence: Synthesises current evidence boundaries. No cost or benefit estimates were collected.
slides.visual: Native options matrix using verbal judgments, no artificial impact scores.
slides.action: Choose the first two research tasks and define the gate for a pilot.
slides.notes: This is the consulting decision. We can confidently recommend a diagnostic and fair comparison because they close specific evidence gaps. The editing pilot is a candidate, not a proven solution. Automated visibility allocation needs a suitable population, calibration, capacity rules and evaluation of who gains or loses. A ranking of slow loans does not tell us which loans would benefit most from extra attention.

slides.title: Make the notebook an argument readers can verify
items: Population, as-of labels, feature blocks and validation contract.
Matched gains, calibration, error slices and text validity.
What is supported, what is uncertain and which test comes next.
slides.message: Each exhibit should answer a question and lead to a bounded interpretation.
slides.evidence: Current walkthrough has specification drift, repeated hardcoded claims and conflicting interpretation.
slides.visual: Three spacious sections with analytical outputs beneath each heading.
slides.action: Refactor around shared src functions and a versioned result manifest.
slides.notes: The next notebook should use the authoritative implementation and put insight next to evidence. Every major exhibit should state what we observe, why it matters and what remains unresolved. We should not repeat hardcoded metrics or describe a later source-validation pass as a complete notebook run. A full-data execution and accepted report bundle will be required before the revised empirical findings are promoted.

slides.title: Test one truthful presentation change
slides.message: A prospective experiment should estimate a defined intervention on all eligible listings.
slides.evidence: Candidate factual clarity/specificity prompt, usual-content control. Assignment, horizon, practical threshold and power are not yet fixed.
slides.visual: Four numbered steps with endpoint and guardrails in a separate short statement.
slides.action: Agree the intervention and observation contract with participating partners.
slides.notes: One candidate is a prompt that makes the existing purpose and use of funds clearer while preserving facts. Compare the offer of that prompt with usual practice and include all eligible listings in analysis. Decide the assignment unit to limit staff/template contamination and marketplace spillovers. Choose one primary completion horizon, a practical effect threshold and sufficient independent units before launch. Do not compare duration only among loans that fund after treatment. Measure accuracy, editing burden, representation and displacement as guardrails. No sample size or duration is justified yet.

slides.title: Advance when each decision has enough evidence
slides.message: The next milestone is a credible comparison, followed by a decision on whether to pilot.
slides.evidence: Research plan with dependency-based gates; no committed delivery dates.
slides.visual: Four horizontal work stages, owners and concrete exit tests.
slides.action: Start with claim correction, outcome availability and the feature-block comparison.
slides.notes: The immediate work is to correct the analytical story and establish a data contract. Next, run the matched full-data benchmark and inspect stability. Then decide whether the remaining uncertainty warrants a pilot, additional data or stopping a proposed feature. Scale only if a prospective practical benefit and acceptable guardrails support it. These are functional owner suggestions, not claims about individual work by Mike or Sophia. The project's contribution is the evidence and the disciplined next decision.

slides.title: Appendix: primary predictive benchmark
rows: Inspect tail error and loss alignment
Needs reliability analysis, not sufficient alone
slides.message: Keep metrics, target units and population together.
slides.evidence: Exact JSON report values; no rerun.
slides.visual: Native benchmark table with negative R² retained.
slides.action: Read complementary metrics and audit the prediction task before deployment.
slides.notes: Primary numeric values are read from the saved report. Ridge trains on log duration and is scored in days after exponentiation. This target/loss choice warrants inspection of tail predictions; a negative R² can coexist with a lower MAE than the baseline. The classifier's negative class is completed funding after 24 hours, not expired or never-funded listings. The historical holdout has already been examined and informed later research, so it is not a fresh untouched evaluation.

slides.title: Appendix: replace claims that exceed the evidence
rows: Text's incremental value needs a matched comparison.
Some narrative associations remain; editing benefit is unestablished.
SHAP describes what the predictive model uses.
We measure listing-to-completion time, often after disbursal.
Sparse regional patterns motivate hypotheses, not geographic advice.
slides.message: Accurate language is part of analytical quality.
slides.evidence: Notebook/deck audit and current evidence map.
slides.visual: Two-column replacement table; historical materials remain preserved.
slides.action: Apply these replacements consistently in notebook prose and future slides.
slides.notes: Several old sentences are stronger than the data allow. The correction should be systematic rather than leaving a careful caveat at the end while overclaiming earlier. Also retire cross-unit coefficient rankings, the unsupported selectivity explanation for period trends, the 20,000-loan topic sample presented as full-data evidence, and claims that a heuristic few-cluster screen is calibrated inference.

slides.message: Complexity follows a demonstrated research need.
slides.evidence: Detailed notebook plan; experiments are not executed.
slides.visual: Ranked work table with concrete gates.
slides.action: Run the inexpensive information and validity checks first.
slides.notes: Sparse linear text baselines and the existing tree family are sufficient to establish a strong starting comparison. Embeddings should respond to a documented measurement or prediction gap. Survival analysis requires censored and unsuccessful listing histories and an explicit competing-event design. Causal forests or double ML do not solve unidentified treatment or missing confounding information merely by being more sophisticated models.
